newsitem.title: CHINA: Chevalier Dev to focus Shanghai housing.
newsitem.headline: Chevalier Dev to focus Shanghai housing.

text.p: Chevalier Development International Ltd (CDIL) said it plans to transfer its Hong Kong housing projects to Chevalier International Holdings Ltd (CIHL) and focus on low cost housing projects in Shanghai.
CDIL has agreed to buy three companies engaged in low cost housing projects in Shanghai from Grand Assets (China) Co Ltd for HK$600 million, the company said in a statement.
The purchase will be paid through the issue of 101.80 million new CDIL shares, or 16.64 percent of its enlarged share capital, at HK$2.658 each and the balance of HK$329.42 million in cash.

CDIL also proposes to transfer its 50 to 100 percent stake in 10 companies, engaged in Private Sector Participation Scheme projects in Hong Kong, and a related management company, to CIHL for HK$530.73 million in cash.
CDIL will sell its stake in three companies engaged in the supply and installation of building materials to CIHL for HK$82.28 million in cash.
CDIL said it would raise net proceeds of HK$283.60 million from the transactions.

CDIL proposes to distribute its 56.23 percent stake in Chevalier Construction Holdings Ltd to shareholders by way of a special dividend in the proportion of one Chevalier Construction share for every four CDIL shares held.
CIHL's stake in CDIL will be reduced to 45.82 percent from 54.97 percent following the series of transactions.
Trading in Chevalier Development, Chevalier International and Chevalier Construction shares was suspended on Tuesday and resumed on Friday.
Chevalier Development rose HK$0.125 to HK$4.00, Chevalier International was up HK$0.15 at HK$2.45 and Chevalier Construction gained HK$0.01 to HK$1.34.
